title: A calculator with precedence
description:
Write `fn eval(src: &str, vars: &HashMap<String, f64>) -> Result<f64, String>` that evaluates arithmetic by recursive descent. Include your own tokenizer (the drill's is fine). The grammar:

```text
expr   = term (("+" | "-") term)*
term   = power (("*" | "/") power)*
power  = unary ("^" power)?          ^ groups from the right: 2^3^2 = 2^9
unary  = "-" unary | atom
atom   = number | name | "(" expr ")"
```

- names are looked up in `vars`; an unknown name is `Err("unknown name 'x'")`;
- dividing by zero is `Err("division by zero")`;
- anything left over after a complete expression, a missing `)`, or a missing operand is an error (any message).
hints: Each grammar rule becomes one method that calls the next rule's method; `power` calls itself for its right side, which is what makes `^` group from the right (lesson 8.05). For the arithmetic itself, `base.powf(exp)` raises one `f64` to the power of another.
After `expr()` returns, check that every token was used; otherwise `1 2` would quietly give 1.
